rows.source: FillInput(): Input[tid*2] = Source(tid) = rotl(Sources[tid%32], (tid/32)*8); Input[tid*2+1] = Previous(tid) = 0xabcd1234 ^ tid*0x01030507 (2 dwords per lane, idxen index tid*2, stride 4 -> byte offset tid*8)

notes: Code is built by constexpr BuildCode<WaveSize>(); words_file is a g++ build of that generator (1491 / 1493 words, matching the manifest).

'words' [8,18) is the EXEC-masked broadcast prologue (v_mov v3,v4; s_mov exec_lo = 0xa5a5a5a5; three in-place v_mov_b32_sdwa v3,v3 BYTE_1/2/3 UNUSED_PRESERVE; then s_mov_b32 exec_lo, -1), so EXEC is all-ones again when the words end.

Every combination c (0..293) in the kernel is 3 ALU words at word 18+5c (v_mov_b32 v6, v5; v_mov_b32_sdwa v6, v4 <sel>) followed by a buffer_store of v6. The stores interleave the ALU words, so post replays the 3 unmodified kernel words of each combination of this slice as .long and replaces its store by v_mov_b32 v(10+k), v6 (see 'segments'). Result 294 is v3 (the broadcast).

Check() asserts all 294 combinations in every lane, and result 294 only when the subgroup holds a wave32 (always on hardware): active lanes (bit tid of 0xa5a5a5a5 / 0x3c3c3c3c) expect byte 0 broadcast, inactive lanes the unchanged source.
The test also runs Wave64Code split into two wave32 halves on the host (ComputeTarget(32)); on the oracle the Wave64Code adapter is the native wave64 run.
verified: disassembly: llvm-mc gfx1030 of the generated words (broadcast block, first/last combinations, and every combination's 3-word pattern asserted by the generator: v_mov_b32 v6,v5 then an sdwa word pair, store offset = 4*c); rows expression checked equal to a g++ build of Source()/Previous()
